questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose to do my Erasmus in Italy because I love the country and wanted the experience of living there and to learn some italian.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a very nice semester, getting to know a lot of new people and traveling within Italy.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a real challenge. Luckily we could contact the Italian coordinator at the university that could provide some help, but most of the information I had to figure out myself or by help from other students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very confusion.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found our apartment through Airbnb and made the lease-agreement outside airbnb to make the monthly rent cheaper. However it was still pretty expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Milano is very expensive so expect rent to be at least 800euros. Another important aspect I wish I knew is that the city is much bigger than the circle showed on the map, so you should definitely look for housing outside the ring, especially the northern part of Milano house a lot of young people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very difficult

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was a big challenge and I had to make my own schedule of classes. I was a big puzzle because I had to consider the amount of ECTS point, when and where the courses takes place. However, the registation of courses can still be done after first week of school, so the students have the opportunity to attend different courses before the final registation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Through their platform, but it was confusing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registation was easy and you don't have to stress about it at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend to chose courses within the same field or major. I took a wide variety of courses which in the end was a bit confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not the most interesting and engaging classes I have experienced.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied but most of the teaching was a bit old school. Several teachers just talk for the entire class while the students just copied what the teacher. A bit boring and monotone. But other teachers also tried to engage the students in discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Wars of Images, British theatre and performance, Cultural history of the modern period, Classical mythology and its media.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked British theatre and performance because the teacher engaged the students a lot and the subject is interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. I had to pay a garage tax to my landlord at the end of my stay, but it was only 15e pr month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Milano is not as cheap as other places in italy but restaurants and groceries are still more cheap than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not hear about anything

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: non I think

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: non

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes, visit cities nearby, the flixbus tickets are very cheap and the traintickets are likewise ok cheap. The many markeds during the week and weekend. Visit the museums and have a look at the events happening in the city, I found a lot of thing through social media.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met people in class, but it was mostly Erasmus students I ended up talking to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not sure

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the Italians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They will figure it out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friendships I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning when I didn't know many people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
